verdict.label: not_comparable
verdict.rationale: The two claims concern different outcomes and different contrasts after the same exposure (RYGB). Claim A reports within-patient weight regain (BMI increase from 29 to 31 kg/m2 between 2 and 5 years post-RYGB), while Claim B reports weight loss from baseline to 12 months (24.1% decrease). Even though both involve body weight/adiposity after RYGB, the outcome time windows and the direction of change differ (late weight regain vs early postoperative weight loss), and neither abstract provides a common comparable contrast (e.g., head-to-head change over the same interval or a shared control group). Because the outcome/contrast is not sufficiently similar, the findings cannot be meaningfully compared.

source_evidence.quote: Between 2 and 5 years after surgery, BMI had increased to 31 kg/m2.
After a 24.1% mean weight loss from baseline to month 12 (P < 0.001), body weight plateaued from month 12 to 24 (-0.9%, P = 0.50).

diagnostics.notes: Both abstracts study RYGB and body weight/adiposity, but Claim A focuses on late weight regain (2 to 5 years) while Claim B focuses on early postoperative weight loss (baseline to 12 months). The outcome measures (BMI vs % weight loss) and time windows differ, and there is no shared comparator or common contrast enabling a meaningful comparison of the two findings.
